items.note: One dinner plate at Amphora Diner, Herndon, Virginia, shown from two angles; counted ONCE. Official menu identifies corned beef, onions, green peppers, potatoes and a hint of tomato; it provides no nutrition for this dish. Restaurant recipe, ingredient proportions and quantities are estimates, not official nutrition. Chunky house-made-style hash modeled from ingredients, not canned hash. Credible high-side model: 170 g cooked corned beef (about 6 oz), 250 g cooked potatoes before griddling, 40 g onion, 40 g green pepper and 30 g tomato raw-equivalent recipe amounts, two large eggs (100 g edible before cooking), plus 20 g retained added cooking fat for the entire hash AND eggs (about 1.4 tbsp oil equivalent). Roughly two generous cups of hash under the eggs; photo cannot determine weight or absorbed fat. One coherent generous serving, not stacked maximum portions. USDA cooked brisket includes intrinsic fat; eggs and potatoes use no-added-fat ingredient bases, with griddle fat counted once separately. Canola oil is only a cooking-fat nutrient proxy; actual oil/butter unknown, so fatty-acid detail is less certain. Added seasoning salt is unknown and not invented; sodium is an ingredient estimate only. No cheese, toast, extra sides or drink counted: toast is mentioned on menu but neither reported nor pictured, and background glass is not a drink report. Dinner classification is user-specified; exact meal time not reported. Assumes this one reported plate consumed.
